name: Chunky pixel art
one_line: Big crisp pixels, sixteen colours, a tiny world seen from above.
look_words: A small world drawn in big, crisp pixels and seen from a raised three-quarter angle. A limited palette of about sixteen colours: grass greens, warm dirt, cream stone, with clear lit and shaded sides on everything. Shading is done with hand-placed dither and a dark one-pixel outline, never with blur or gradients. Light is a warm afternoon. Yellow and sky blue mark pickups and the goal, red is harm, and the player is pale cream with a dark outline. Shapes are chunky and readable at a glance. Motion is in steps: two or three frames for a walk, things that pop rather than fade. Avoid smooth scaling, rotation that breaks the pixel grid, soft shadows and bloom.

palette.name: sixteen colours
palette.notes: Use the base colours and their shades only; a pixel look falls apart when extra in-between colours creep in.

upgrade.why: real pixel art from a 3D scene: a small render, an exact palette, a camera that snaps to whole pixels

music.mood: bright chiptune with a soft bass

sound_feel: short square-wave blips, a soft noise burst for steps

Cosy and readable. Gameplay view of a stylised indie video game, no text, no user interface, no logos, no watermark.
